$comment: Trusted in a Kotlin value written into HTML, judged by both editors alike: Trusted offered as a fix in element text and where it is not, a literal or raw-string Trusted read as the markup it writes, in a call to interpolate, in a val set to one and in a Kotlin template, so the values after it are judged where they really land; a Trusted whose text is not known leaves what follows it uncertain; a name declared Trusted or set to Trusted(...) is Trusted. A case may give `constants`, the workspace's const val names.

cases.name: a String in element text: the rewrite and Trusted, neither preferred
cases.source: fun layout(body: String) = "<main>$body</main>"

issues.message: Kotlin writes $body into the HTML as it is. If it can hold text from outside, build the string with interpolate(...), which escapes it; if it is markup you built, declare it Html or wrap it in Trusted(...).
fixes:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate

fun layout(body: String) = interpolate("<main>%s</main>", body).text

cases.name: a Trusted a Kotlin template writes into the format is read as format
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.Trusted fun f(x: String) = interpolate("
${Trusted(x)}
")

issues.message: Kotlin fills in ${Trusted(x)} before interpolate reads the markup, so interpolate reads what it holds as markup too: a %s in it is a placeholder and a %% a per cent sign, and interpolate throws or changes the markup. Make it a %s placeholder and pass the Html: interpolate writes an Html or a Trusted there as it is.
fixes:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.interpolate import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.Trusted fun f(x: String) = interpolate("
%s
", Trusted(x))

cases.name: an empty Trusted before a value fixes nothing, and interpolate always throws on the value
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.*
fun f(q: String) = interpolate("<script src=\"%s%s\"></script>", Trusted(""), q)

issues.message: interpolate always throws here: q lands in src, which loads code from wherever the value points, and the markup before it does not fix the host. Only Trusted(...) is let in there. Start the value with a path such as /js/ or a whole origin such as https://cdn.example/, so that the value only picks a file there, or wrap a URL you chose yourself in Trusted(...).

cases.name: a literal Trusted attribute name puts the value in a Datastar expression
cases.source:
import io.github.markusaugust.streamlord.core.domain.*
fun f(q: String) = interpolate("<button %s=\"%s\">Go</button>", Trusted("data-on:click"), q)

issues.message: interpolate always throws here: q lands in data-on:click, which Datastar runs as an expression or follows as a signal path, and only a number or a boolean is let in there. Put the value in an attribute of its own, such as data-label, and read it in the expression with el.dataset.label.

cases.name: a literal Trusted attribute name in a Kotlin template puts the value in a Datastar expression
cases.source: fun f(q: String) = "<button ${Trusted("data-on:click")}=\"$q\">Go</button>"

issues.message: Kotlin interpolates $q here, as the whole Datastar expression. Meant as a server value, only a number or a boolean is safe there; meant as the signal $q, make the whole literal $$"""...""" (Kotlin 2.2+), or escape as ${'$'}q.
fixes:
fun f(q: String) = $$"<button $${Trusted("data-on:click")}=\"$q\">Go</button>"
fun f(q: String) = "<button ${Trusted("data-on:click")}=\"${'$'}q\">Go</button>"
fun f(q: String) = "<button ${Trusted("data-on:click")}=\"\$q\">Go</button>"

cases.name: a literal Trusted tag name in a Kotlin template puts the value in code
cases.source: fun f(q: String) = "<${Trusted("script")}>$q</${Trusted("script")}>"

issues.message: Kotlin writes $q into a script, which the browser runs, so escaping does not help. Put the value in a data-* attribute and read it from there.

cases.name: a literal Trusted src in a Kotlin template loads code from wherever the value points
cases.source: fun f(q: String) = "<script ${Trusted("src")}=\"$q\"></script>"

issues.message: Kotlin writes $q into src, which loads code from wherever the value points, and the markup before it does not fix the host: even an https:// URL can load code from another origin. Escaping does not help. Start the value with a path such as /js/ or a whole origin such as https://cdn.example/, so that the value only picks a file there.
